questions.question: Arrange in increasing order: n², n log n, 2ⁿ, log n, n.
questions.solutionApproach: Bucket classification: log < poly (by degree) < exponential. log n < n < n log n < n² < 2ⁿ.
questions.answer: log n < n < n log n < n² < 2ⁿ

questions.question: Which grows faster: n^(log n) or (log n)^n?
questions.solutionApproach: Take log of both: log(n^(log n)) = (log n)². log((log n)^n) = n·log(log n). Compare (log n)² vs n·log(log n) — as n→∞, n grows far faster than (log n), so n·log(log n) dominates (log n)². Hence (log n)^n grows faster.
questions.answer: (log n)^n grows faster than n^(log n).

questions.question: Is it TRUE that f(n)=O(g(n)) implies g(n)=Ω(f(n))?
questions.solutionApproach: f=O(g) means f(n)≤c·g(n) eventually, which directly rearranges to g(n)≥(1/c)·f(n) eventually — exactly the definition of g=Ω(f). TRUE (this one, unlike O⟹reverse-O, actually IS always true).
questions.answer: TRUE — f=O(g) and g=Ω(f) are the SAME statement viewed from two sides.

questions.question: for(i=1;i<n;i=i*2){ for(j=0;j<n;j++){ /* O(1) work */ } }  What is the overall time complexity?
questions.solutionApproach: Outer loop: i doubles each time from 1 to n → runs O(log n) times. Inner loop: runs O(n) times, independent of outer. Nested → multiply: O(n log n).
